record.paper_title: Exploring Progressions: A Collection of Problems
record.original_question: Let a, b, and c be nonzero real numbers that are consecutive terms of a harmonic progression. Prove that the three numbers a − b/2, b/2, and c − b/2 are consecutive terms of a geometric progression, and give two numerical examples.

evidence.quote: Show that if the nonzero real numbers a, b, c are consecutive terms of a harmonic progression, then the numbers a − b/2, b/2, c − b/2, must be consecutive terms of a geometric progression. Give two numerical examples.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Three nonzero real numbers $x, y, z$ are said to be consecutive terms of a harmonic progression if their reciprocals $1/x, 1/y, 1/z$ form an arithmetic progression, i.e. $\frac{2}{y} = \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{z}$. Three real numbers $u, v, w$ are said to be consecutive terms of a geometric progression if $v^2 = u\,w$ (with $u, w$ allowed to be of the same sign so that the common ratio is real).

Let $a, b, c$ be nonzero real numbers that are consecutive terms of a harmonic progression. Prove that the three numbers
$$a - \tfrac{b}{2},\quad \tfrac{b}{2},\quad c - \tfrac{b}{2}$$
are consecutive terms of a geometric progression; that is, show
$$\left(\tfrac{b}{2}\right)^2 = \left(a - \tfrac{b}{2}\right)\left(c - \tfrac{b}{2}\right).$$
Also provide two explicit numerical examples of triples $(a,b,c)$ illustrating the statement.
artifact.status_search_result: This is an elementary algebraic identity exercise. Starting from $2ac = b(a+c)$ (the harmonic condition $2/b = 1/a + 1/c$), one expands $(a-b/2)(c-b/2) = ac - (b/2)(a+c) + b^2/4 = ac - ac + b^2/4 = b^2/4$, which is the geometric-progression condition. The problem is a classical textbook exercise and is considered solved.

status_evidence.title: Harmonic progression (mathematics) - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Numbers a,b,c are in harmonic progression iff 2/b = 1/a + 1/c, equivalently 2ac = b(a+c).
status_evidence.claim: Standard definition allows direct verification of the identity (b/2)^2 = (a-b/2)(c-b/2).
